sentences.asr_text: Questions six to ten are based on part two of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Is the phenomenon of parent and kids studying together at university a rare case?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 父母和孩子一起上大学，这种现象少见吗？

sentences.en: I am afraid not.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 恐怕并不少见。

sentences.en: Changing careers later in life is no longer a rarity, so it is not uncommon for students and their parents to be toying with the big decisions at the same time.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 在人生后期转行已经不是什么稀罕事了，因此，学生和父母同时考虑重大决定也并不少见。

sentences.en: Class surveys indicate that the majority of Harvard alumni have shifted directions when it comes to their careers.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 班级调查显示，大多数哈佛校友在职业发展中都曾改变方向。

sentences.en: With the financial collapse of 2008, such shifts have become more widespread.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 2008年金融危机之后，这种转变变得更加普遍。

sentences.en: Students have seen their family members lose jobs or change them.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 学生们见过家人失业或转行。

sentences.en: Gone is the time when you start out at a company and work there for the rest of your life.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 从进入一家公司起就在那儿工作一辈子的时代，已经过去了。

sentences.en: So your mom started study again just because she wanted to change her career?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 所以，你妈妈重新开始学习，就是因为她想转行吗？

sentences.en: Yes, she used to be in the real estate industry but now she wants to be a lawyer.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 是的，她以前从事房地产行业，现在则想成为一名律师。

sentences.en: Does her experience affect you somewhat?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 她的经历会对你产生一些影响吗？

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Freshman Week, in one of the welcoming speeches, our dean mentioned that many of us might have grown up thinking that “doctor, lawyer, teacher” were our only options.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 新生周的一次欢迎致辞中，院长提到，我们很多人可能从小就认为“医生、律师、教师”是仅有的职业选择。

sentences.en: She urged us to stick to our dreams.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 她鼓励我们坚持自己的梦想。

sentences.en: But later I realized talking about passions is one thing—actually following them is another.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 但后来我意识到，谈论热爱的事情是一回事，真正去追随它们则是另一回事。

sentences.en: By the time I started to think about what professional directions I might want to take, I had heard “The average American changes careers seven times” so often that it was hard not to become numb to its message.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 当我开始思考自己可能会选择怎样的职业方向时，“美国人平均一生会转行七次”这句话我已经听得太多，几乎对此麻木了。

sentences.en: The last thing that the enthusiastic Harvard student wants to do is to imagine moving from job to job until she lands somewhere by chance, especially when the economy is so uncertain.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 一个满怀热情的哈佛学生，最不愿意想象的，就是自己在不同工作间辗转，直到碰巧落在某个岗位上，尤其是经济如此不确定的时候。

sentences.en: My mom can serve as a good example.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我妈妈就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Even if she graduated from Harvard herself as a brilliant student, she had to make alterations of her career.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 即使她当初也是以优异成绩从哈佛毕业，也仍然不得不调整自己的职业方向。

sentences.en: So, is your mom actually happy studying with younger students?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，你妈妈和年轻学生一起上课，真的开心吗？

sentences.en: Hard to say.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 很难说。

sentences.en: Frustration is routine for older students, you know, who have to learn how to study all over again.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 对年长的学生来说，挫败感是家常便饭，因为他们得重新学会如何学习。

sentences.en: Mom once described the experience of taking classes with students half her age after 30 years in the workforce: “What’s most challenging is that you come into class knowing how to make a cake—but you’re all there to make omelets.”
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 妈妈曾这样描述自己工作三十年后，和年龄只有自己一半的学生一起上课的经历：“最有挑战的是，你走进教室时已经知道怎样做蛋糕了，但大家在这里学的却是做煎蛋卷。”

sentences.en: A kind of wasting time?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 有种在浪费时间的感觉？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Do you think your mom has played an important role in shaping your idea of what kind of person you want to be?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你觉得，在形成自己想成为什么样的人的观念时，妈妈发挥过重要作用吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Harvard offers many resources for students who want to figure out where their future lies.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 哈佛为想弄清未来方向的学生提供了许多资源。

sentences.en: Advisers, tutors, and OCS keep their doors open to help undergraduates embark on this kind of discovery.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 学业导师、辅导老师和职业服务办公室都敞开大门，帮助本科生开始这样的探索。

sentences.en: One can’t find one’s passions in a booklet on summer internships or a list of possible career paths.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 一个人无法仅凭一本暑期实习手册，或一张可能的职业道路清单，就找到自己的热爱。

sentences.en: It’s a gradual process that involves sharing thoughts and then coming back to them; a discussion that doesn’t always have its end goal in mind.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这是一个循序渐进的过程，需要交流想法，再回过头来思考；这样的讨论并不总是一开始就有明确的终点。

sentences.en: In the course of my time at Harvard, it has been just such a give-and-take—with professors, with friends, and with my mother—that has slowly shaped my ideas of who I might want to be.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 在哈佛求学期间，正是和教授、朋友、妈妈之间这样的思想交流，慢慢塑造了我对未来想成为怎样的人的认识。

sentences.en: I really cherish the time she spent together with me at university.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我非常珍惜她和我一起在大学度过的时光。

sentences.en: Well, Maggie.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 好的，玛吉。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for staying with us today.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天和我们聊了这么多。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: This is the end of part two of the interview.
sentences.zh: 访谈的第二部分到此结束。

sentences.speaker: W

sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第8题：工作三十年后重返课堂，玛吉的妈妈有什么感受？

sentences.en: Question 9. What is most challenging for Maggie’s mom?
